report: Team D1 Benchmark Report - Post-Fix Re-Testing
purpose: Re-test recommendation system after run-001 fixes: entry_node filtering, related fallback, success-weighted scoring

SOP-011.note: Pattern-based recommendation returned route starting from SOP-011 (score=1.0)

SOP-012.note: No pattern match for SOP-012 entry; fell back to strength-based routing from SOP-012. Returns pointers FROM SOP-012, not a global route.

SOP-017.note: Pattern-based recommendation returned route starting from SOP-017 (score=1.0)

SOP-023.note: No pattern match for SOP-023 entry; fell back to strength-based routing from SOP-023.

SOP-027.note: No pattern match for SOP-027 entry; fell back to strength-based routing from SOP-027.

entry_node_filtering.summary: All 5 entry points return results rooted at the specified entry node. No global route leakage observed. Fix #1 confirmed working.

SOP-011_novel_task.note: SOP-011 has a primary pointer (SCR-0019), so primary tier returned first. Related fallback not exercised because primary exists.

SCR-0006_related_only.note: SCR-0006 has ONLY related pointers (no primary/supporting). System correctly falls through to related tier and returns useful results. Fix #2 confirmed working.

related_fallback.summary: Related-strength fallback works correctly. When a node has no primary or supporting pointers, the system falls through to related pointers and returns useful results.

novel_task_no_entry.output: Best-connected SOP: SOP-028 with 8 primary/supporting pointers: ['SOP-027', 'SOP-G02', 'SOP-015', 'SOP-024', 'SOP-025', 'SOP-023', 'SCR-0013', 'SOP-029']
novel_task_no_entry.note: With no entry_node and no pattern history, system searches all SOP nodes and returns the best-connected one. Fix #3 confirmed working.

no_entry_fallback.summary: No-entry-node fallback correctly searches all SOP nodes and returns the best-connected SOP (SOP-028 with 8 primary/supporting pointers).

benchmark_test_scoring.setup: Logged 3 routes via path A (SOP-011 -> SCR-0019 -> KB-0025) with 'failure' outcome; 2 routes via path B (SOP-011 -> SCR-0030 -> SCR-0032) with 'success' outcome.
benchmark_test_scoring.note: Path B recommended despite lower frequency (2 vs 3) because score = count * success_rate. Path B score (2.0) > Path A score (0.0). Fix #4 confirmed working.

success_weighting.summary: Success-weighted scoring correctly prioritizes routes with higher success rates over more frequently-used but failing routes.

non_existent_node.output: No route recommendation available for task='test', entry='SOP-999'
non_existent_node.note: Graceful handling, no crash, returns None.

empty_task_string.note: Falls through to strength-based routing. No crash.

wiki_node.note: No WIKI-prefixed nodes exist in the current pointer network.

src_node.note: SRC nodes work as entry points. Returns primary pointers from the SRC node.

kb_node.note: KB nodes work as entry points. Returns primary pointers.

accuracy_score.justification: All four fixes (entry_node filtering, related fallback, no-entry fallback, success-weighted scoring) are confirmed working correctly. The system handles edge cases gracefully without crashes. Score reduced from 10 because: (1) the no-entry fallback finds the best-connected SOP by pointer count but does not consider task relevance -- it always returns SOP-028 regardless of task type; (2) empty task string is handled but could benefit from explicit validation; (3) the pattern-based entry_node filtering only matches routes where the route string starts with the entry node text, which could break if a node ID is a prefix of another (e.g., SOP-01 matching SOP-011).

remaining_issues.issue: No-entry fallback always returns SOP-028 regardless of task
remaining_issues.description: The no-entry fallback selects the SOP with the most primary/supporting pointers globally. It does not consider task keywords or context. This means every novel task without an entry_node gets the same recommendation.

remaining_issues.issue: Entry node pattern matching uses string prefix check
remaining_issues.description: The entry_node filter uses route.startswith(entry_node), which could false-match if one node ID is a prefix of another (e.g., 'SOP-01' would match 'SOP-011 -> ...'). Current node naming convention avoids this, but it is fragile.

remaining_issues.issue: No input validation on empty task strings
remaining_issues.description: An empty task string is silently accepted and processed. Could benefit from a warning or early return.

remaining_issues.issue: WIKI nodes do not exist in the pointer network
remaining_issues.description: Cannot test WIKI node edge case. Not a bug, just a gap in test coverage.
